- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean or 0.5–1.0 price point.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often over-anticipates continuation; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum after 2–3 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model often under-responds; add 0.5–1.0 price point lag correction or increase downward bias.
- Model frequently underestimates mean reversion in 30-day horizon; if recent 18-day mean is >82.0, forecast should be >82.0; if <78.0, forecast should be <78.0.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture volatility; add ±0.5–1.0 price point buffer around forecast for 3–5 day horizon.
- If true outcome shows early sharp drop after spike, model often fails to recognize “sell-off” sentiment; reduce forecast by 1–2% of recent peak or 0.5–1.0 point for next 3 days.
